text:
jamie: quick Q re: chat-completions contract change — Dan's PR adds per-message `meta` field and flips toolcall param ordering for streaming deltas. Is that safe for SDKs? I worry about clients that expect positional assumptions and nullable role semantics. PR: https://git/repo/pull/420

sasha: can you paste example payload? :eyes:

jamie: sure — current vs proposed:

```
// current
{ "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"...","tool_call":{"name":"search","args":["q","k"]}}]}

// proposed
{ "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"...","meta":{"source": "ui"},"tool_call":{"args":["q","k"],"name":"search"}}]}
```

omar: flipping `name`/`args` ordering is fine for JSON semantics but some stream parsers assume stable key presence ordering for delta assembly. Which SDKs parse stream by token position vs object keys?

ryan: Node SDK v2 reads `tool_call.name` from the first delta chunk and then accumulates `args` in subsequent chunks; it expects `name` to show up early. That could break if deltas reorder keys. We should either keep ordering in streaming delta events or add a normalization shim server-side.

devex-bot: Suggested mitigation: add runtime flag `toolcall_key_ordering=preserve` for 2 weeks and run client-compat tests. See runbook: https://confluence/repo/runbooks/toolcall-compat-checks :thinking:

jamie: SG. Proposal: runtime adds a tolerant parser to accept either ordering (normalize on ingest) + schema validator warns on unknown top-level per-message fields (soft-deprecate). We can also emit a warning header in the stream for older SDKs. Thoughts? :shrug:

sasha: agree. also add a smoke test in the streaming test suite that sends toolcall deltas with swapped keys and verifies reassembly. I can add that test.

omar: I'll add fallback in the C++ streaming consumer to handle either `name`-first or `args`-first. Should be a tiny change. Omar++ :thumbsup:

ryan: ping me when the shim PR lands, I'll update Node SDK tests and run a quick release candidate.

jamie: Plan + timeline: runtime PR https://git/repo/pull/420 (shim + flag), node sdk PR https://git/repo/pull/88 (tests). Enable `toolcall_key_ordering=preserve` behind flag for 1w on canary, monitor toolcall failure rate in Console (alert if >0.1%). If stable, flip default after 7 days and schedule flag removal in 30 days. :rocket:

ci-bot: deploy-prod started for runtime/shim v.r123 at 4809993456 — good luck!

jamie: thanks all, will follow up with canary metrics and a short postmortem if anything flares up.
